entities.summary:
Criminology is a modern Idea born in the early 20th century, studying the causes and manifestations of crime. The field emerged as a response to the growing concern over crime rates and social disorder in urban centers. This led to the establishment of the first criminology departments in universities, staffed by scholars such as Cesare Beccaria and Enrico Ferri, who sought to understand the root causes of crime and develop evidence-based policies to prevent it. Their work influenced the development of the criminal justice system and shaped the way societies approach crime and punishment.

The core events in the history of criminology include the 1911 establishment of the first criminology department at the University of Rome, the 1920s rise of positivist criminology, and the 1950s development of modern criminology as a distinct field of study. These events produced a shift in focus from punitive approaches to crime to more rehabilitative and preventive strategies. This legacy can be seen in contemporary debates over mass incarceration, restorative justice, and community-based crime prevention programs.

Criminology's significance lies in its ability to shape our understanding of crime and its impact on individuals, communities, and societies. By studying the causes and consequences of crime, criminologists have helped inform policy decisions and public health initiatives aimed at reducing crime rates and promoting social cohesion. The field's evolution has also influenced the development of related disciplines, such as forensic psychology and sociological criminology.
